newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: "Self-enrichment" motive for Slovak dam - Hungary.
newsitem.headline: "Self-enrichment" motive for Slovak dam - Hungary.

text.p: Hungary told the International Court of Justice on Monday Slovakia's diversion of the Danube for a hydroelectric power project was an illegal act of self-enrichment which was harming the environment and depriving Hungarians of vital water resources.
"These acts were a serious violation of the territorial sovereignty of Hungary," Foreign Ministry lawyer Gyorgy Szenasi told the United Nations court.
Szenasi was speaking on the first day of court hearings on a long-running dispute over the Gabcikovo dam project which has led to strained relations between Budapest and Bratislava.
The Slovak dam was originally part of a 1977 plan agreed by the then communist governments of Czechoslovakia and Hungary.
But Budapest suspended work on a companion dam downstream at Nagymaros in 1989, following pressure from environmental groups, and in 1992 pulled out of the project altogether.
Slovakia went ahead with the hydroelectric scheme at Gabcikovo but agreed to submit the dispute to the U.N. court.
Hungary says it abandoned the project because of concerns about the effect on water supplies and the environment.
Reduced water-flow and falling ground water levels, it says, have had a devastating effect on the flora and fauna of the Danube's flood plains, as well as on agriculture and fisheries.
"It is the character and control of that river, its sustainability for future generations, and nothing less, that is the essential issue for the court," Szenasi said.

Hungary says Slovakia's unilateral diversion of a river forming part of their common border violates international law and it should be ordered to pay compensation. It calls electricity production with Danube river water "illegal self-enrichment".
But Slovakia argues Hungary failed to implement its part of the agreement and should therefore pay damages to Slovakia. It will present its case to the court at the end of this month.
The court, the main judicial organ of the United Nations, is expected to deliver its ruling in the autumn.
